**ID:** Pvr 1.1
**Section:** Parivāra (pvr)
**Collection:** Vinaya

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Katthapaññattivāra* ("Questions and answers on the monks’ Monastic Code and its analysis") forms the opening section (Pvr 1.1) of the *Parivāra*, the analytical and pedagogical concluding division of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The treatise systematically expounds the origin and promulgation circumstances of each disciplinary rule prescribed for Buddhist monks. It also incorporates an important sequence of mnemonic verses detailing the lineage of Vinaya masters through whom the monastic discipline was transmitted. An English translation of the text has been made available by Bhikkhu Brahmali. The text is related by cross-reference to several other canonical loci, notably the *Upālisutta* (AN 10.31), the subsequent nuns' *Katthapaññattivāra* (Pvr 2.1), and the *Atthavasapakaraṇa* (Pvr 9).

Textual reuse data computed by DharmaNexus demonstrates that the *Katthapaññattivāra* shares voluminous formulaic material across the Vinaya corpus [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali tradition, its most substantial passages are shared with its counterpart Pvr 2.1 (exceeding 9,000 matches), as well as other sections of the *Parivāra* such as Pvr 1.9, Pvr 2.9, and Pvr 18, and commentarial works including the *Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā* and *Parivāra-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Across language traditions, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages of the text with diverse Northern monastic materials, including Sanskrit manuscripts of the *Prātimokṣasūtra*, the *Adhikaraṇavastu*, and the *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya*, alongside Tibetan canonical texts such as the *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D 5) and the *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati* (D 4104) [DharmaNexus].
